proofParity: eth_getProof byte sizes are near-identical across clients at every milestone — 3.5× p50 8,071 B (NM) vs 8,072 B (Geth); 5× mean ~11.4 KB on both — exactly as expected for the same state root. EIP-1186 proofs are client-agnostic, so witness size is comparable regardless of which client serves it.
summary: Across both milestones the two clients land at opposite optima. Geth serves reads with a several-× lower tail (3.5×: aggregate p99 22 ms vs 160 ms; 5×: 110 ms vs 360 ms) on ~2.4–3× lighter memory; Nethermind pushes ~2.5–3× the gas throughput and keeps a ~25–30% smaller on-disk DB. The read-latency win is Geth's, the block/gas-execution win is Nethermind's — and the split holds as the state grows.
workMatched: One caveat colours the read-latency numbers: latency is coupled to import duty cycle. At 3.5× the latency shown is the 60-minute run; at 5× it's the 5-minute run, because the 5× 60-minute run was NOT work-matched — Geth imported ~1,300 blocks vs Nethermind's ~560 (≈2.3× the work, and far heavier blocks by the end), which pushed Geth's 60-minute read tail to ~520 ms while Nethermind (throttled by memory pressure) sat at ~180 ms. A cleaner 60-minute Geth re-run reproduced this exactly — 1,301 blocks, aggregate p99 520 ms, RSS flat at ~42 GB as GC keeps pace. At the equal-work 5-minute mark Geth's tail (~110 ms) was well below Nethermind's (~360 ms). The honest cross-client statement is per unit of work: Geth stays the lighter, lower-tail reader; Nethermind the higher-throughput executor. A block-count-capped run is the open item that fully decouples the two.
caveat: Gas/s is not a strict like-for-like statistic — Geth reports a decaying go-metrics timer, Nethermind a gauge — treat it directionally. The read window (recent_block_window=8–64) sits inside both clients' served-state window. Paired Geth-vs-NM execution/RPC is measured at 3.5× and 5×. Single-client pinned-window runs now reach higher milestones: Geth executes the 10× state (3.35 TB) at ~881 MGas/s with p99 13 ms reads and ~18 GB RSS, flat for an hour; Nethermind executes 7× (3.04 TB) at ~1,490 MGas/s — both without any state-scale collapse (an earlier x7 slowdown was traced to a memory-conserving GC config, not state depth). Matching cross-client pairs at 7× / 10×, and the Besu / Reth / Erigon clients, are still pending (issues #21 / #26). Nethermind runs use the daniil/rpc-readpath-perf build; Geth v1.17.4 (chainId-patched).
